ukotveni: Gebo moves by exchange, and counts nothing as arrived until it has gone both ways.
text: Under the slipping ground there is one hold that does not slip. Eihwaz is what stays fastened while the surface goes. And it does not hold for nothing — it counts nothing as arrived until it has gone both ways; the root takes the weight and the slope gives it back something to grip.

Under the loose ground one hold does not give. Eihwaz is what stays fastened when the surface will not. There is a reciprocity in it — the slope leans on the root and the root leans back, meeting halfway, an exchange neither side arranged.

Under the sliding ground one hold does not slide. Eihwaz is what stays fastened when everything above it moves. The slope pushes and the root answers — not more, not less. What the ground does, the root does back, and the face of the hill holds because of it.
